our-squad.headline: Our gameweek 6 squad: Cole Palmer captains a 3-4-3
our-squad.standfirst: The engine's own 15 — a 3-4-3 projecting 56.74 points with the captain doubled, picked on six-gameweek horizon value, not one-week form.
our-squad.body_html:
This is the team we actually field, and it stands or falls in public. The engine optimises expected points over a discounted six-gameweek horizon on market-implied scoring rates, so every pick is a horizon bet rather than a one-fixture spike. The XI lines up 3-4-3 and projects 51.52 points before the armband; with Cole Palmer doubled that becomes 56.74.

No Haaland, by conviction rather than oversight. At his price the model wants the budget spread across three lines, and we do not pay a premium for an ownership shield. If the crowd is right about him, the consensus XI on this site owns him and will collect the evidence.

Cole Palmer wears the armband because he tops this squad's doubled projection at 10.44 — captaincy here is expected value, never narrative. Szoboszlai is vice: if the captain's match falls through, the armband moves to the next-best number, not to a hunch.

The bench, in order: 1. Sánchez, 2. E.Le Fée, 3. Bobby Thomas, 4. Shaw. It is deliberately thin — the first name is the backup keeper, and the spend sits in the XI where the points are.

distributions.headline: Gameweek 6 spreads: Saka hauls 40% of the time
distributions.standfirst: Every projection on this site is the average of tens of thousands of simulated gameweeks. This is the shape behind the average: Saka blanks in 21% of them and scores double figures in 40%.
distributions.body_html:
Saka (ARS) projects 15.93 with the armband. Behind that one number: his floor is 2 points in the worst tenth of simulations, his single most likely score is 2, and his ceiling is 16 in the best tenth. He reaches double figures in 40% of simulations and returns two points or fewer in 21%.

B.Fernandes is the alternative at 14.31 captained, on a floor of 1 and a ceiling of 15. He outscores Saka in 44% of simulated gameweeks. That comparison treats the two players as independent of each other. They are not: two attackers in the same match rise and fall together, and our simulation knows it even though this figure does not. Read it as the size of the gap, not as a settled number.

Saka holds both ends of the board this week: the highest floor (2) and the highest ceiling (16). That is unusual, and it is the case for taking him.

consensus-squad.headline: The consensus XI: the experts' gameweek 6 team
consensus-squad.standfirst: A mention-tally across the expert consensus sources, assembled into a legal 15 — Haaland carries the majority armband.
consensus-squad.body_html:
This squad follows the crowd on purpose. We tally which players the expert consensus sources keep naming, keep the names most lists agree on, and assemble them into a quota-, budget- and club-legal 15. The captain is the majority call, not ours: Haaland, with João Pedro as vice.

Its minutes come from sourced research notes rather than our engine — where the experts assert a starter, this squad believes them. The weekly gap between this team and our own squad measures exactly whose information about who actually plays is better.

Scored on our numbers, the 3-4-3 XI projects 41.86 points, 48.36 with the captain doubled. Both squads are published before every deadline and graded after it — the season scoreboard settles the argument.
